questions.stem: What is the union of two sets A and B?
choices: The set of all elements common to A and B
The set of all elements in A or B but not both
The set of all elements in A and B
The set of all elements in A or B including those in both
questions.solution: The union of two sets A and B is the set of all elements that are in A or B, including those that are in both. The correct answer is 'The set of all elements in A or B including those in both'. The other options describe the intersection, symmetric difference, and a general set, which are not the definition of union.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about sets?
choices: A set is a collection of objects that are not well-defined.
A set which contains no elements is called a finite set.
A set which contains a definite number of elements is called an infinite set.
A set which does not contain any element is called an empty set.
questions.solution: The correct statement is that a set which does not contain any element is called an empty set. This is accurate because an empty set is defined as a set with no elements. The other options are incorrect: a set must be well-defined, a set with a definite number of elements is finite, and an infinite set has an uncountable or indefinite number of elements.

questions.stem: What does the symbol φ represent in the context of sets?
choices: A finite set
An infinite set
An empty set
A universal set
questions.solution: The symbol φ represents an empty set, which is a set containing no elements. A finite set has a specific number of elements, an infinite set has an unending number of elements, and a universal set includes all elements under consideration in a particular context.

questions.stem: What is the set-builder form of the set {1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...}
choices: {x : x is a prime number}

{x : x is an even number}
questions.solution: The correct answer is {x : x = n², where n ∈ N}, which represents the set of squares of natural numbers. The other options do not accurately describe the given set. {x : x is a prime number} and {x : x is an even number} do not match the pattern of the set. {x : x is a natural number} is too general and does not specify the square relationship.

questions.stem: If set A is a subset of set B and A ≠ B, then what is A called?
choices: Proper subset
Superset
Equal set
Singleton set
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Proper subset' because when set A is entirely contained within set B but is not equal to it, A is defined as a proper subset of B. 'Superset' would describe B in this relationship, 'Equal set' implies A and B have exactly the same elements, and 'Singleton set' refers to a set with only one element, which is unrelated to the relationship described.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the set A = { x : x ∈ R and x satisfy x² – 8x + 12 = 0 }?
choices: A is an empty set.
A contains all real numbers.
A contains exactly two elements.
A contains infinitely many elements.
questions.solution: The equation x² – 8x + 12 = 0 is a quadratic equation, which can be factored into (x – 2)(x – 6) = 0, giving two real solutions, 2 and 6. Therefore, the set A contains exactly two elements. An empty set would have no solutions, containing all real numbers would require an identity, and infinitely many elements would imply a non-unique or continuous solution set, which does not apply here.
